The invention relates to a reciprocating piston engine having at least one length-adjustable connecting rod coupled to a crankshaft. The connecting rod comprises a first rod part and a second rod part that can be telescopically displaced relative to one another by means of a length-adjustment device. This telescopic movement changes the effective length of the connecting rod and thereby allows the compression ratio of the engine to be adjusted.

A control valve is provided to selectively connect the length-adjustment device to an oil pressure line or isolate it from the oil pressure line. By controlling the supply and discharge of pressurized oil, the valve enables the connecting rod to be extended or shortened as required.

The control valve is electrically switchable and is actuated inductively. For this purpose, a stationary magnet device arranged on the engine induces an electric current in an induction device mounted on the connecting rod. The induced current supplies the energy needed to switch the control valve without requiring a direct electrical connection to the moving connecting rod.

This arrangement provides a simple, compact, and reliable mechanism for varying the effective connecting-rod length. It also allows flexible adjustment of the engine’s compression ratio in response to different operating conditions, thereby supporting improved efficiency, performance, and emissions behavior.
outputs.L4:
A reciprocating piston engine may be equipped with a telescopically length-adjustable connecting rod to vary the engine’s compression ratio during operation. The connecting rod includes at least two components that can move relative to one another and a hydraulic adjustment mechanism supplied with engine oil. By selectively directing or blocking the oil flow between hydraulic chambers, the mechanism changes or fixes the effective length of the connecting rod. Increasing the connecting-rod length raises the piston’s top-dead-center position and therefore increases the compression ratio, while shortening the connecting rod lowers the compression ratio.

Oil flow within the adjustment mechanism is controlled by an electrically switchable valve integrated into the connecting rod. Because the connecting rod moves rapidly with the piston and crankshaft, supplying electrical energy through conventional wires or sliding contacts would be difficult and susceptible to wear. Electrical energy is therefore generated inductively in a device mounted on the connecting rod. A magnetic field produced by a stationary magnet arranged on the engine housing, or by a magnet mounted on the crankshaft, passes the connecting-rod-mounted device during engine rotation and induces an electrical current. That current can directly actuate the valve or charge an energy-storage element that powers the valve at the required time.

When the valve is switched, it changes the hydraulic connection between the oil-filled chambers of the telescopic connecting rod. The forces acting on the piston and connecting rod then cause the movable rod components to shift toward a selected length. Once the desired position has been reached, the valve closes or hydraulically locks the chambers so that the connecting rod retains its adjusted length under engine loads. Depending on the design, the system may provide two defined connecting-rod lengths or permit adjustment among several positions.

The inductive arrangement eliminates the need for complex electrical wiring to the moving connecting rod and reduces reliance on mechanically actuated switching components. It can be implemented with few parts, requires little installation space, and is protected by the connecting-rod structure and the engine lubrication environment. The resulting system provides a simple, compact, and reliable way to alter the effective connecting-rod length and thus vary the engine’s compression ratio according to operating conditions. A high compression ratio can be selected to improve efficiency at low or moderate loads, while a lower compression ratio can be used at high loads to reduce knock tendency and protect the engine.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the most common words in the English language. Though small, it plays an important role by identifying a specific person, place, object, or idea. For example, “a book” may refer to any book, while “the book” points to a particular one.

This simple word brings clarity and precision to communication. It helps listeners and readers understand exactly what is being discussed. Often overlooked, “the” demonstrates how even the smallest elements of language can have a significant impact.

A hydraulic control circuit includes an electrical control valve arranged to control a flow of hydraulic fluid to and/or from the hydraulic chamber. The control valve includes an inductively actuated valve element movable between at least two switching positions in response to an electromagnetic field generated by an induction device positioned adjacent to a movement path of the connecting rod. An electronic controller selectively energizes the induction device in coordination with an operating position of the engine, thereby contactlessly actuating the control valve and adjusting the effective connecting-rod length. The arrangement enables variation of a compression ratio and/or piston stroke while reducing or eliminating wired electrical connections to the moving connecting rod.

counterfactuals.prompt: How could a connecting rod’s hydraulic control valve be powered without wiring, batteries, or slip contacts while keeping a variable-compression engine compact and reliable? Answer in formal patent language and include numbered reference signs.
counterfactuals.output:
**Energy-Autonomous Hydraulic Connecting-Rod Assembly**

A connecting-rod assembly **(10)** for a variable-compression internal-combustion engine comprises a connecting-rod body **(12)**, an eccentric adjustment mechanism **(14)** arranged at a small-end bearing **(16)** or a large-end bearing **(18)**, and at least one hydraulic chamber **(20, 22)** operatively connected to the eccentric adjustment mechanism **(14)**. A hydraulic control valve **(24)** selectively controls hydraulic-fluid flow between the hydraulic chambers **(20, 22)** and an engine lubrication circuit **(26)**.

An energy-conversion device **(30)** is mounted on or incorporated into the connecting-rod body **(12)** and is configured to convert cyclic mechanical loading of the connecting rod **(12)** into electrical energy. The energy-conversion device **(30)** may comprise a piezoelectric element, magnetostrictive element, electromagnetic microgenerator, or combination thereof, disposed in a region subjected to alternating tensile, compressive, bending, or inertial loading during engine operation.

The generated electrical energy is supplied through an integrated rectifier circuit **(32)** to an energy-storage element **(34)**, preferably a capacitor or supercapacitor. The energy-storage element **(34)** powers an electrically actuated valve actuator **(36)** associated with the hydraulic control valve **(24)**. The valve actuator **(36)** may comprise a low-energy latching solenoid, piezoelectric actuator, or bistable microactuator, such that electrical power is required substantially only when changing the switching state of the hydraulic control valve **(24)**.

A contactless command receiver **(40)** is arranged on the connecting-rod assembly **(10)** and is configured to receive control commands from a stationary or crankcase-mounted transmitter **(42)**. Communication may be effected magnetically, inductively, acoustically, optically, or by radio-frequency transmission. A local controller **(44)** actuates the valve actuator **(36)** in response to the received command and an available-energy signal from the energy-storage element **(34)**.

Accordingly, the hydraulic pressure required to reposition the eccentric adjustment mechanism **(14)** is provided by the engine lubrication circuit **(26)**, while only the comparatively small switching energy of the hydraulic control valve **(24)** is generated locally. No external electrical wiring, electrochemical battery, brush arrangement, or slip contact is required between the engine structure and the moving connecting-rod assembly **(10)**.

The energy-conversion device **(30)**, rectifier circuit **(32)**, energy-storage element **(34)**, receiver **(40)**, and controller **(44)** are preferably received within sealed recesses **(46)** of the connecting-rod body **(12)** and encapsulated by an oil-resistant dielectric material **(48)**. This arrangement provides a compact, mechanically protected, and substantially maintenance-free control system suitable for the high acceleration, temperature, and lubricant exposure occurring within the crankcase.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a technical invention summary for an internal combustion engine whose connecting rod changes length to vary compression ratio. Explain that the valve connects or isolates the adjustment mechanism from an oil-pressure line and receives induced electrical current when the rod passes a fixed magnetic device.
counterfactuals.output:
### Technical Invention Summary

The invention relates to an internal combustion engine having a variable-length connecting rod for changing the engine’s compression ratio. The connecting rod includes a hydraulically actuated adjustment mechanism configured to alter the effective distance between the crankpin and the piston pin. Changing this distance varies the piston’s top-dead-center position and thereby adjusts the compression ratio.

A valve incorporated into or carried by the connecting rod selectively connects the hydraulic adjustment mechanism to, or isolates it from, a pressurized engine-oil line. When connected, oil pressure actuates or repositions the adjustment mechanism. When isolated, hydraulic fluid is retained so that the connecting rod remains at its selected effective length.

The valve is electrically operated without requiring a continuous wired connection to the moving connecting rod. A stationary magnetic device is positioned adjacent the path of the connecting rod. As the rod passes the magnetic device during engine rotation, the changing magnetic field induces an electrical current in a coil or other conductive element mounted on the rod. The induced current energizes the valve, causing it to switch between its connecting and isolating states. The magnetic device may be selectively activated or controlled so that valve operation occurs during a predetermined crank-angle window.

This arrangement enables compression-ratio adjustment using existing engine-oil pressure while avoiding slip rings, flexible wiring, or other direct electrical connections to the reciprocating and rotating connecting rod assembly.
